question.problem: The price of a new bicycle is $$625.$ If the bicycle loses $\frac{1}{5}$ of its value every year, what will be its value after $4$ years?

current_example.problem: A radioactive substance decays exponentially such that its mass reduces by  $\dfrac 1 3$ every year. If the mass of the substance was initially  $4\,\textrm{kg},$  what is the mass of the substance after $6$ years?
current_example.worked_solution:
If the mass of the substance reduces by $\dfrac 1 3$ every year, then $\dfrac 2 3$ of its mass remains every year.

Therefore:

- After $1$ year, the mass is $4\cdot \left(\dfrac 2 3\right)\,\textrm{kg}.$

- After $\color{blue}2$ years, the mass is $4\cdot \left(\dfrac 2 3\right)^{\color{blue}2}\,\textrm{kg}.$

- After $\color{blue}3$ years, the mass is $4\cdot \left(\dfrac 2 3\right)^{\color{blue}3}\,\textrm{kg}.$

- $\ldots$

Repeating this pattern, we see that the mass after $\color{blue}6$ years is $4\cdot \left(\dfrac 2 3\right)^{\color{blue}6}\,\textrm{kg}.$
